# onboarding_applications

Onboarding applications records in Operations Desk. Product articles define their operational scope.

Read this collection using `search_records(resource="onboarding_applications", filters={}, cursor=0, limit=20)` or `get_record(resource="onboarding_applications", record_id="<returned id>")`.

**Filters:** exact scalar equality; in, contains, gte and lte operator objects on supported top-level fields. See DB-query-syntax for type and null behavior.

Search returns selected summary fields, so omission from a summary is not proof of absence from the complete record. Read detail before interpreting an optional field. Fields depend on the record type and processing stage; null and absent fields are not zero amounts. Types below describe public record shapes, rather than mandatory properties on every row.

## Fields

| Field | Observed public types | Search use | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `billing_account_id` | string | Top-level filter | Billing account id: opaque identifier reference. Its target depends on the containing record/operation; do not infer a collection merely by pluralizing the field name. Explicit joins are listed separately. |
| `bundle_id` | string | Top-level filter | Bundle id: opaque identifier reference. Its target depends on the containing record/operation; do not infer a collection merely by pluralizing the field name. Explicit joins are listed separately. |
| `business_area` | string | Top-level filter | Business area: public attribute of this record type. The associated service article defines its operational use. |
| `commercial_reference` | string | Top-level filter | Reference supplied by a commercial source; use the source and period when matching evidence. |
| `direct_controllers` | array | Top-level filter | Direct controllers: list of the named business attributes or references; inspect all entries relevant to the record. |
| `entity_id` | string | Top-level filter | Entity id: opaque identifier reference. Its target depends on the containing record/operation; do not infer a collection merely by pluralizing the field name. Explicit joins are listed separately. |
| `id` | string | Top-level filter | Opaque record key used by get_record; obtain it from returned records or explicit references. It is not an amount, date or proof of business identity. |
| `missing_subjects` | array | Top-level filter | Missing subjects: list of the named business attributes or references; inspect all entries relevant to the record. |
| `ownership_threshold_bp` | integer | Top-level filter | Ownership threshold rate in basis points: 100 bp = 1%, 10,000 bp = 100%. The product rule specifies the amount to which the rate applies. |
| `published_registry_review_minute` | integer | Top-level filter | Published registry review minute: logical minute or duration, as indicated by the field name; compare with get_clock and the applicable event/validity terms. |
| `review_delay` | integer | Top-level filter | Review delay: public attribute of this record type. The associated service article defines its operational use. |
| `review_due_minute` | integer | Top-level filter | Review due minute: logical minute or duration, as indicated by the field name; compare with get_clock and the applicable event/validity terms. |
| `reviewed_minute` | integer | Top-level filter | Reviewed minute: logical minute or duration, as indicated by the field name; compare with get_clock and the applicable event/validity terms. |
| `scope` | string | Top-level filter | Access namespace for the record. It is not a customer name or a universal case_id. |
| `status` | string | Top-level filter | Current state of this particular object. A proposal or submission state is distinct from a posted payment or completed review. Public values represented here: `APPROVED`, `DRAFT`. This list describes the documented records, not an input-validation enum. |
| `submission_fee_minor` | integer | Top-level filter | Submission fee amount, in integer minor units of the applicable currency. Inspect this record type and its source/receipt to distinguish declared values from actual movements. |


## Product entry points

| Product / record model | Starting collection | Related records |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Trade Services and typed Payment services | service_cases | service_records by case_id; service_bookings for executed operations. Parent kind selects DB-service-<kind>. |
| Operations Desk: commercial receivables | desk_portfolios | trade_invoices, remittances, remittance_advice and invoice_allocations. |
| Operations Desk: corporate onboarding | onboarding_applications, entities | company_profiles, ownership_edges, evidence_bundles and submissions. |
| Operations Desk: collection rails and account exit | rail_sites, desk_accounts | rail_profiles, rail_bindings, desk_services and billing_instances. |
| Operations Desk: treasury and card loss | treasury_obligations, card_loss_cases | treasury_mandates, loss_components, compensation_entries and card_disputes. |
| Operations Desk: restricted funds and batch payments | restricted_lots, payment_batch_items | fund_restrictions, receivable_rights, purpose_instructions, submission_attempts and bank_receipts. |
| Operations Desk: currency delivery and tax | currency_obligations, tax_transfers | fx_routes, fx_quotes, fx_trades, tax_periods, tax_allocations and message_amendments. |
| Reserve funding facilities | reserve_routes | reserve_disbursements and the explicitly referenced destination desk_accounts. |
| Joint capital for typed services | joint_agreements | joint_sources, joint_routes and joint_fundings by agreement_id. |
| Contract links between typed services | link_contracts | primary_case_id and secondary_case_id reference service_cases. |

These are distinct record models. service_cases is not a universal directory for Operations Desk accounts, invoices or onboarding. A service_cases query with no results does not require trying its sibling collections. Use the product's documented starting collection. desk_accounts holds Operations Desk wallets; generic accounts is a separate inherited product interface. A title or ordinary customer name is not an internal record ID.
